name: Auggie

surfaces.label: Child agent of a self-hosted Cosmos daemon, Auggie 0.x: the daemon spawns `<node> <auggie entry> [--augment-*] cloud run-as-agent <agentId> --workspace <dir> --parent-daemon-id <id> ...` per session (augment.mjs 0.36.0). The parent `auggie daemon` process is deliberately NOT matched (it holds no turn of its own); each child is matched and judged on its own direct children. The id after run-as-agent is a cloud agent id, not a conversation id. Auggie 1.x uses a different argv, see the next surface.

Child agent of a self-hosted Cosmos daemon, Auggie 1.x (npm tags daemon and preview): the daemon spawns `<node> <auggie-v2.mjs> [--augment-*] --cloud-agent <agentId> --workspace-root <dir> --parent-daemon-id <id> ...`. There is NO `cloud run-as-agent` in this argv (1.x only rewrites that legacy form into --cloud-agent when typed by hand). `--cloud-agent` alone also marks a hand-started Cosmos agent process, which is a session too. The parent `auggie daemon` is not matched.

Auggie in ACP mode, launched through the npm bin shim: `node .../bin/auggie --acp [--workspace-root <dir>] [--model <m>]`, spawned by an editor (Zed, Neovim, Emacs ACP clients per docs) or by the Augment VS Code extension's sidecar (extension 0.901.1 spawns `auggie --acp --workspace-root <dir>`). One process can hold several ACP sessions. 1.x also accepts `--mode acp`, which is NOT matched (the token `acp` cannot be tested as a whole word).

Same ACP mode, node started directly on the package file (`node .../node_modules/@augmentcode/auggie/augment.mjs --acp` or `.../auggie-v2.mjs --acp`), the shape an editor extension that resolves the package uses.

auggie --print (or -p, not matchable: args_contain is a substring test and '-p' hits '--mcp-config' and any path containing '-p'): one instruction, then exit. Alive means working. Matched on the long flag only, and only when argv also carries the shim path (`bin/auggie`) or the package path, so an unrelated `node script.js --print` in a folder named auggie is not picked up. `auggie -p ...` runs are therefore NOT seen (known gap).
Same print mode, node started directly on the package file.

Auggie in a terminal, launched through the npm bin shim: `node /opt/homebrew/bin/auggie` or `node ~/.nvm/versions/node/<v>/bin/auggie` (env-shebang launch keeps the symlink path as argv[1]; inferred, no live process seen). Covers 0.x (augment.mjs) and 1.x (auggie-v2.mjs). Exact-argument vetoes drop MCP-server mode, ACP, print mode, the daemon, `cloud` subcommands, 1.x daemon children (`--cloud-agent`, `--parent-daemon-id`) and 1.x `--mode <text|json|rpc|acp>` runs (rpc and acp are host-driven helpers, not human sessions; `--mode` is 1.x only). Short admin subcommands (login, upgrade, session list, ...) are NOT vetoed: ps args are split on spaces, so a veto on a word like `list` or `model` would also drop a session started with a prompt containing that word. Such a subcommand shows up as a brief idle session. The same applies to the words `daemon` and `cloud`: a prompt containing them as separate words is dropped.

Same, node started directly on the package file: `node .../node_modules/@augmentcode/auggie/augment.mjs` (0.x) or `.../auggie-v2.mjs` (1.x). This is the shape the daemon itself uses when it re-spawns (process.execPath + resolved entry).

Augment extension for VS Code (augment.vscode-augment) and JetBrains: the Agent panel runs inside the IDE process. No separate process carries it, so nothing here can be matched; only the ACP sidecar above and the bundled one-shot migration engine (out/migration-engine/auggie-v2.mjs) are visible, and the latter is not a session. bundle_ids left out on purpose: the host app's bundle id would mark every VS Code window as Augment.
Cosmos cloud sessions (Augment-hosted sandbox VMs, web app). No local process. `auggie cloud ...` only manages them.

session_store.note: 0.x (npm latest, 0.36.0). One JSON file per conversation, rewritten whole (temp file `.write-<id>.json.<ts>-<rand>.tmp` then rename), not an append log; `<id>-backup<N>.json` siblings also match the glob. The file is saved after every committed exchange (onExchangeCommitted), on loop complete, error and interrupt, so mtime moves per model round-trip, never per token. Root moves with `--augment-cache-dir`. Top-level keys (from the writer in the bundle, no local file seen): sessionId, created, modified, chatHistory, agentState, rootTaskUuid, workspaceId, remoteCreatedAt, title, customTitle, terminalId, subAgentCreditsUsed, subAgentCostUsd, summarizations, plus optional subAgents, poseidonAgentId, parentConversationId, isCloudAgent, queue (saveSession object literal, augment.mjs 0.36.0). terminalId holds the output of `tty` (for example /dev/ttys012), which is the one process-to-session link: match the process's controlling tty to terminalId and take the newest file. It is only set when stdin is a tty, so daemon children and piped print runs carry no usable terminalId (an earlier value is kept on re-save). `--resume <prefix>` accepts an unambiguous id prefix, so an id read from argv may not equal the file name. `--dont-save-session` writes nothing. Do not read chatHistory.

stores.surface: Auggie 1.x (npm tags preview and daemon, 1.2.0-prerelease.*): a fork of pi-mono's coding agent
stores.path: ~/.augment/sessions-v2/--<cwd, leading / dropped, every / \ : replaced by ->--/<sessionId>.jsonl (AUGGIE_CODING_AGENT_DIR or --augment-cache-dir moves the root, --session-dir the folder)
stores.note: First line is a header {type:session, version, id, timestamp, cwd, parentSession}. Appended per finished entry and not created until the first assistant message ends. `--session <path>` takes a FILE path, not an id, so it must not go in session_id_args. In 1.x `--resume`/`-r` is a picker flag (help text 'Select a session to resume'), so `session_id_args: --resume` on a 1.x process may read a prompt word as an id; the lookup then finds no file and nothing is lost.

working_signals.meaning: The shell tool (`launch-process` in 0.x, `bash` in 1.x) starts each command as a detached `<shell> -c <command>` DIRECT child of the node process (0.x: child_process.spawn(cmd, [], {shell, detached:true}); 1.x: spawn(shell, [-c ...], {detached:true})). A shell child means a tool call is running. Blind while the model streams. Caveats: an MCP stdio server configured with useShellInterpolation is a long-lived `/bin/sh -c` child; hook scripts run as short shell children. Inferred from source, no live process seen. 1.x also has an opt-in `--enable-terminal` (AUGGIE_ENABLE_TERMINAL=1); whether it leaves a persistent shell child was not traced.

0.x: ~/.augment/sessions/<id>.json is rewritten after each committed exchange and at loop end, so a fresh mtime raises working. A long model call or a long tool call leaves it quiet, so absence proves nothing. 1.x: the jsonl gains a line per finished message.

Guess, nothing measured because Auggie is not installed here. The Ink TUI redraws while a response streams; a turn waiting on the network burns almost none. Risk of false working: both lines run a workspace indexing worker thread (indexing-worker.mjs in 1.x, indexing in 0.x) inside the same process, so a fresh session that is indexing can exceed the floor while idle. Treat as a last resort.

waiting_signals.meaning: 0.x with settings notificationMode = desktop_notification: when the agent needs input it runs `osascript -e 'display notification "Agent needs your input" with title "Augment Agent"'` through child_process.exec, so a sub-second direct child (or its /bin/sh wrapper) whose args carry that text. Turn end uses 'Agent response complete'. Too short-lived for polling; a process-start event would catch it. Off by default in the config wizard state (notificationMode: off).

0.x with notificationMode = bell writes BEL to the tty both when the agent needs input and when it finishes; the two are not distinguishable. `--no-bell` disables it. Changelog: 'Terminal Bell: Now correctly rings when the agent is waiting for user input' and 'Notification Bell on Ask-User'.

No hook is a usable wait signal. `Notification` is accepted in settings.json and listed in the docs' hook_event_name field, but the 0.36.0 bundle defines onNotification and never calls it (2 hits: the definition and a no-op stub). Tool approval prompts and the 1.x ask-user extension are invisible from outside the process.

hooks.config: hooks key in ~/.augment/settings.json (user), <workspace>/.augment/settings.json (project), <workspace>/.augment/settings.local.json (personal), /etc/augment/settings.json (managed, highest precedence; C:\ProgramData\Augment\settings.json on Windows). Handler type is only `command`; the script must end in .sh, .ps1, .cmd or .bat and be executable with a shebang; timeout in ms, default 60000. Event JSON arrives on stdin.
hooks.note: The docs page describes five events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionStart, SessionEnd). The 0.36.0 schema accepts seven. PromptSubmit is undocumented but firePromptSubmitHook runs when a user message is sent (turn start, payload user_prompt). Stop carries agent_stop_cause: end_turn, interrupted, max_iterations, error, and fires on user interrupt too, so PromptSubmit then Stop brackets a turn. Notification is declared and never fired in 0.36.0. Hook input fields: hook_event_name, conversation_id (the session id), workspace_roots. PreToolUse and PostToolUse also run inside sub-agents (0.30.0). 1.x accepts the same seven names in its config schema; firing was not traced. Cursor-style names (beforeShellExecution, stop, ...) are accepted and mapped.

telemetry.how: NOT in npm latest 0.36.0: its OpenTelemetry packages are Sentry's instrumentation and no OTLP exporter or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* read exists. In 1.x (npm tags preview and daemon, 1.2.0-prerelease.*) the `otel` extension exports metrics, logs and traces over OTLP (grpc, http/protobuf default, http/json): enable with AUGGIE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1, CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 (accepted as an alias) or `--enable-otel`, endpoint from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT and per-signal variants, off by default. Events include auggie.user_prompt, auggie.api_request, auggie.tool_result, auggie.tool_decision, auggie.session.count, auggie.active_time.total. Needs a collector; not a live signal for a monitor.

notes: No local run was possible, so every process shape is inferred from docs and the published npm bundles. Two generations share one command name. npm latest is 0.36.0 (the Node/Ink CLI, augment.mjs, JSON sessions under ~/.augment/sessions). The 1.x line (auggie-v2.mjs, JSONL sessions under ~/.augment/sessions-v2, OTLP export) is only published as prerelease tags (preview, daemon); expect it on daemon hosts first. The row is written to match both. Nothing outside the process says 'waiting on the human' unless notificationMode is on. The best outside signal for a turn is a direct shell child (tool running) plus a fresh session file; neither covers a long model stream. Hook-based tracking needs PromptSubmit then Stop, and PromptSubmit is undocumented. Verified by a second pass (2026-09-29): the 1.x daemon child argv differs from 0.x (no `cloud run-as-agent`), so it has its own surface; `-p` runs and `--mode acp|rpc` runs stay unmatched by design; tree_cpu is an unmeasured guess and indexing can trip it. Not covered: the Intent macOS app (intentapp.dev, its own daemon `intentd`, hosts Augment and other CLI agents; bundle id and process names unknown) and the Cosmos web app. Both look like separate rows or hosts.
